$comment: Public release history and known issues (spec §11A, docs/SUPPORT.md §8). DoMe for Windows 0.1.0 is published as a free beta (GitHub release v0.1.0, 2026-11-13, the release in src/content/windows-release.json); nothing in it is Windows-device-tested or iPhone-tested, and Screen view is in the program but switched off for accounts on domeremote.com. Every entry is honest about verification. Rendered by src/pages/public/ReleaseNotesPage.tsx.

status.headline: DoMe for Windows 0.1.0 is published as a free beta. This release has not been verified on a Windows 10 or 11 PC or on an iPhone yet.
status.verification: Automated tests run on every component (unit and integration, with simulated Windows and phone behavior), and the signed Windows installer was tested on GitHub’s Windows Server test machine. Real iPhone and real Windows PC checks are listed as pending below; nothing on this page claims they passed.

changes: The first official download of DoMe for Windows: DoMe-Setup-0.1.0.exe, with its SHA-256, on the Download page and the GitHub release page. It is signed for Windows by Justin Gaskins through Azure Artifact Signing and installs for your Windows account only.

In this version: the touchpad and keyboard (with the permissions you grant each phone on the PC), Windows media and volume, approved apps, Lock, confirmed Sleep, Restart and Shutdown, and pairing phones by QR code with approval on the PC.
Not in this version: YouTube control in Chrome or Edge. The DoMe browser extension is not in the Chrome or Edge stores yet, and Setup says so.
Screen view (beta) is in the program, but it is not switched on for DoMe accounts yet, so it cannot be used.
Free: nothing can be bought yet. The licence terms Setup shows are still a draft, like this site’s Privacy notice and Terms of service.
verified: Integration-tested on GitHub’s Windows Server test machine (an administrator account with UAC off): install, upgrade and uninstall of the signed Setup, and the signatures on Setup and the installed program.
Unit-tested on GitHub’s Windows test machine: the PC app’s automated tests.
Every file on the GitHub release was compared with the checked build (SHA-256) before the release was published.
The version information behind the Download button is signed with DoMe’s update key, and this site checks that signature when it is built.
not_verified: Install, upgrade and uninstall on a Windows 10 or 11 PC, and by a standard (non-administrator) user.
Windows 11 PCs with Smart App Control on.
Everything listed as not verified for the builds below: no check on a real Windows PC or a real iPhone has been recorded for this release.

changes: Free touchpad and keyboard: cursor movement, clicks, double click, right click, scrolling, explicit Drag mode, literal typing with a Compose and Send fallback, tested shortcuts (Ctrl+A/C/V/Z, Ctrl+L in browsers).
Explicit, independently revocable touchpad and keyboard permissions per phone, granted by the PC owner on the PC; existing pairings do not receive them automatically.
Connection health screen with one next action per state, a first-use walkthrough, and help links from every failure.
Support requests from the app with a reference number after receipt and a copyable redacted summary when sending fails.
Now Playing panel showing exactly which PC, app or browser tab a media control will affect.
Sleep, restart and shutdown confirmations state that remote access can end and that remote wake is not supported.
Ask: an optional AI butler, off until you turn it on. Speak or type a request; only requests DoMe can’t work out by itself go to Anthropic’s AI, and the phone shows every step it runs.
verified: Unit and component tests in the phone app (jsdom), the PC agent (simulated Windows adapter) and the relay (real PostgreSQL).
not_verified: Real iPhone Safari / installed PWA gestures, keyboard varieties (IME, autocorrect, dictation, emoji), rotation and backgrounding.
Real Windows input injection, multi-monitor and mixed-DPI behavior, lock screen and UAC restrictions.
Network loss during a drag, key hold or text send on real devices.
Installer, update and uninstall on Windows 10/11.
Ask on a real iPhone: speech recognition, spoken replies and AI requests against the live AI service.

changes: YouTube control through the browser extension in a background tab (not in the published DoMe for Windows 0.1.0), Windows media sessions and system volume, approved apps, Lock, confirmed Sleep/Restart/Shutdown.
Pairing by QR code with local approval on the PC; per-phone signing keys; revocation.
verified: Component test suites and an end-to-end relay-path test between the real services on one machine.

known_issues.title: Windows may warn about DoMe while this version is new
known_issues.detail: DoMe for Windows 0.1.0 is signed by Justin Gaskins, but Windows may still show “Windows protected your PC” while this version is new.
known_issues.workaround: Check that the publisher the dialog names is Justin Gaskins before you continue. DoMe never asks you to turn off antivirus or other protection.

known_issues.title: Not yet verified with Smart App Control
known_issues.detail: It has not been verified yet whether DoMe runs on a Windows 11 PC with Smart App Control on. It may be blocked there: only the DoMe programs, Setup and the uninstaller are signed, not the libraries that come with them.
known_issues.workaround: If Smart App Control blocks DoMe, do not turn Smart App Control off: Windows cannot switch it back on without resetting the PC. Tell us through Support instead.

known_issues.title: No YouTube control in Chrome or Edge in this version
known_issues.detail: The DoMe browser extension is not in the Chrome or Edge stores yet, so DoMe for Windows 0.1.0 does not include YouTube control in Chrome or Edge.

known_issues.title: Screen view is not switched on yet
known_issues.detail: Screen view (beta) is in DoMe for Windows 0.1.0, and the GitHub release page lists it, but it is not switched on for DoMe accounts yet, so it cannot be used. It has not been verified on a device either.

known_issues.title: Linking the PC to your account takes one command
known_issues.detail: DoMe’s menu has no “Link this PC” item yet. Until the PC is linked, the menu says “Not linked — run DoMe link”.
known_issues.workaround: Open Windows PowerShell (not as administrator), run & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\DoMe\DoMe.exe" link | Out-Host, then on the Link a PC page that opens, check the code, name the PC and click Link this PC.

known_issues.title: DoMe for Windows does not check for updates yet
known_issues.detail: This version does not look for newer versions by itself.
known_issues.workaround: When the Download page lists a newer version, download it and run its Setup over the old one. Setup keeps your link, paired phones and settings.

known_issues.title: Double tap on the touchpad relies on Windows’ double-click timing
known_issues.detail: Two quick taps send two clicks; Windows combines them into a double click within its own double-click time (500 ms by default). On a slow connection the second click can arrive late and count as a separate click.
known_issues.workaround: Use the Double button under the touchpad, which sends a true double click.

known_issues.title: Live typing pauses after some edits
known_issues.detail: Correcting text in the middle of what was already sent, or deleting an emoji or accented cluster, cannot be mirrored safely on the PC. Live typing then pauses with an explanation; nothing is sent.
known_issues.workaround: Fix the text on the PC, or use Compose and Send for the rest.

known_issues.title: The phone cannot see which field has focus on the PC
known_issues.detail: DoMe shows the window in front, not the field inside it. Typing goes to whatever the PC has focused.
known_issues.workaround: Click the field on the PC (with the touchpad) before typing.

known_issues.title: Lock screen, sign-in and administrator prompts cannot be controlled
known_issues.detail: Windows refuses remote input on protected screens by design, and DoMe does not try to bypass that.
known_issues.workaround: Unlock or answer the prompt at the PC.

known_issues.title: Freshness is re-evaluated every 5 seconds
known_issues.detail: After the PC goes quiet, controls can stay enabled for up to 5 seconds past the 75-second freshness limit.
known_issues.workaround: None needed; the next state report re-enables them.
